title: Republicans Seize on a Budget Exemption to Push Through Immigration Enforcement Funding
partialText: Republicans are using a special mechanism that was created to reduce deficits to push through immigration enforcement funds that should be provided in a regular spending bill.

title: Federal Panel Approves Trump’s Plans for a 250-foot Arch in Washington
partialText: The panel, whose members were selected by President Trump, has an advisory role on the design of the project but no enforcement power.

title: Trump’s Fund Shows Blanche Choosing Loyalty Over Pushing Back
partialText: Once seen by some as the most conventional of President Trump’s political appointees, Todd Blanche has taken off the gloves in his new role as acting attorney general.

title: Republicans Balk at Trump Fund, Weighing Ways to Limit It
partialText: G.O.P. senators were exploring using their immigration bill to fence off a fund the president wants to tap to pay people who claim government mistreatment.

title: Democrats’ Midterm Strength Masks Fierce Divides and Frustration, Poll Shows
partialText: Democratic voters are in a combative, anti-establishment mood, unhappy with their party and disagreeing about its best path forward, a New York Times/Siena poll found.

title: Experimental Drug Yields Dramatic Weight Loss
partialText: People who got the injection, retatrutide, lost 28 percent of their body weight on average after 80 weeks, Eli Lilly said.

title: Stephen Colbert’s Final ‘Late Show’ Marks the End of an Era
partialText: Stephen Colbert’s “Colbert Report” satirized politics. Then his “Late Show” confronted a moment when politics became self-satirizing.

title: Supreme Court Permits Lawsuits Over U.S. Assets Seized by Cuba in 1960
partialText: The Trump administration backed lawsuits brought by the Havana Docks Corporation that would allow the U.S.-owned entity to get compensation for property confiscated by Fidel Castro’s regime.

title: In Blackout-Hit Cuba, Word of U.S. Castro Indictment Spreads Slowly
partialText: While many Cubans were divided over the legitimacy of the U.S. charging Raúl Castro with murder, the hope for developments that might ease their suffering is widespread.

title: He Sued the N.Y.P.D. He Advised ‘Homeland.’ Now He’s Mamdani’s Lawyer.
partialText: Ramzi Kassem is accustomed to challenging authority. As the chief counsel to Mayor Zohran Mamdani of New York City, he finds himself on the other side.

title: A Powerful El Niño Is Forming. If History Is a Guide, It Could Hit Hard.
partialText: The biggest episodes of the past have altered the course of human events, according to researchers. An emerging one is drawing historic comparisons.

title: Fan A.I. Videos Help Spencer Pratt Break Through in L.A. Mayor’s Race
partialText: Supporters have created A.I. videos to boost the mayoral campaign of Spencer Pratt, the former MTV star. Some videos have gone viral, but it’s not clear whether they will yield votes.

title: Gov. Gavin Newsom to Sign Executive Order Aimed at A.I. Job Loss
partialText: Gov. Gavin Newsom issued an executive order to explore an overhaul of labor policies to deal with potential mass job displacement from artificial intelligence.

title: Thousands of N.Y.C. Jobs Could Be Lost to A.I. Boom, Report Says
partialText: A report by the New York City comptroller argues that the city’s economy will be transformed by artificial intelligence. “We’ve never seen anything like this,” he said.

title: Elon Musk and Other CEOs on Trump’s Trip to China Sought Relief
partialText: Elon Musk and other powerful executives who accompanied President Trump to China are hoping to clear roadblocks put up by Beijing.

title: Trump Approved a Nvidia Chip for Sale in China. Beijing Doesn’t Want It.
partialText: The U.S. tech giant’s powerful H200 chip seemed poised to boost Beijing’s A.I. ambitions, but not a single one has been purchased in China.

title: How Banks Battled for $1 Billion in Fees From SpaceX Listing
partialText: Across Wall Street, bankers have been clamoring to lead what is expected to be the biggest-ever initial public offering.

title: The Hard-Line Military Fraternity Running Iran
partialText: Decision making in the country is guided by a small group of men associated with the Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps.

title: Germany Indicts Two Men for Plotting to Kill Jewish Leaders on Iran’s Behalf
partialText: European authorities have grown concerned about a rise in Iranian intelligence activity in Europe in the wake of the U.S.-Israeli war in Iran.

title: Elim Chan Becomes First Female Music Director of San Francisco Symphony
partialText: Elim Chan has been named the symphony’s next music director. She joins a small field of female conductors at American orchestras, as San Francisco rebuilds after Esa-Pekka Salonen.

title: Uganda Restricts Travel with Congo Over Ebola Outbreak
partialText: Uganda said that flights to and from the Democratic Republic of Congo would be temporarily suspended, as the outbreak appeared to spread to a rebel-controlled province in Congo.

title: Air France Flight to U.S. Is Diverted to Montreal Over Congolese Passenger Amid Ebola Fears
partialText: An Air France plane was sent to Montreal because a passenger from the Democratic Republic of Congo was on board. The U.S. has closed its borders to recent visitors to the African country.

title: How Mamdani’s Budget Announcement Went Viral Far Beyond New York
partialText: Mayor Zohran Mamdani’s executive budget was met with hero worship online. What did the social media chatter miss about the messy reality of municipal policymaking?

title: Mira Nair Finds a New Audience as Mother of Zohran Mamdani
partialText: “I feel like we have given him to the world,” the filmmaker said in a conversation with The New York Times. Her next movie is about one of India’s greatest artists.

title: Bone Found Near Guthrie Home Predates Her Disappearance by 750 Years
partialText: Archaeological experts say the discovery is a cautionary tale about the consequences of citizen investigators taking matters into their own hands.

title: World Cup Fever Brings More Soccer Pitches to N.Y.C.
partialText: Companies, government organizations, nonprofits and schools work to make pitches available to play.

title: New Jersey Says Yes to Airbnbs During the World Cup
partialText: As New York City tamps down on short-term rentals, some New Jersey municipalities are encouraging residents to take advantage of the windfall World Cup travelers could bring.

title: Trump Just Took Us Somewhere the Country Has Never Been Before
partialText: There’s no telling where this leads.

title: A Defense of a Liberal Arts Education in the Age of A.I.
partialText: Making the case for a “useless” education.

title: Intraparty Conflict
partialText: We look at the turmoil inside both political parties.

title: Charges Dismissed for Ex-Assistant Principal After Shooting by 6-Year-Old
partialText: Prosecutors had argued that Ebony Parker, a former assistant principal at a Virginia elementary school, had failed to act on warnings that a child had a gun in his backpack.

title: Is Museum Wall Text the Next Political Battleground?
partialText: The Smithsonian has changed or eliminated some interpretive language that typically accompanies exhibited artworks. Critics call this self-censorship.

title: In Berlin, Cars Are a Culture War Flashpoint
partialText: With municipal elections approaching, conservatives and progressives are sparring over congestion in the city center and how to fix it.

title: Retailers Say Squeezed Shoppers Are Focused on Deals
partialText: Walmart, Target and TJ Maxx recently reported increases in sales, but shoppers are seeking out low-price items and cutting back in some categories, a potentially worrying sign for the U.S. economy.
